summary: The agent implemented the Node-side size-limit paths, but omitted the browser/XHR implementation and used a multipart helper signature incompatible with the delegation verifier. Baseline tests passed; five new tests failed.

details.reasoning: The requested limits apply to the library's Request API, whose base is mixed into both Node and browser implementations. The patch adds the shared methods and Node stream handling but makes no change to src/client.js. Consequently XHR upload/download progress never checks either limit, aborts, or invokes the ETOOLARGE callback; all three browser verifier cases time out. The node multipart helper also accepts (req, formData), while the delegation verifier wraps it as a formData-only prototype method, causing a TypeError. The browser omission alone is enough to fail the explicitly requested feature.
details.secondary_factors: The multipart verifier assumes a formData-only helper signature that is not written explicitly in the prompt, so that particular failure is narrower than the main browser omission. The agent also modified two existing tests to add regressions, but did not alter the hidden verifier or fake functionality.

quick_failure_summary: Browser requests do not enforce request or response size limits, and the multipart delegation helper fails when wrapped by the verifier.

justification.issue_description: Missing browser/XHR enforcement for maxRequestSize and maxResponseSize: oversized browser uploads and downloads neither abort nor callback with ETOOLARGE.
justification.evidence: The prompt requires that 'the request' abort for both maxResponseSize and maxRequestSize without limiting the work to Node. src/request-base.js identifies itself as functions 'shared between node and client code'; both src/node/index.js and src/client.js mix in RequestBase. src/client.js has its own Request.prototype._end and XHR upload/download progress handling, yet it is absent from changed_files.txt and the patch. junit_new.xml reports three 10-second timeouts in 'Client-side maxRequestSize and maxResponseSize'.
justification.verdict_reasoning: This is FAIL_MISSED_REQUIREMENT because cross-runtime request behavior is explicit in a library containing visible Node and client transports, and the shared-base design makes the need to wire the browser transport reasonably foreseeable. It is not a test-harness failure: the browser tests load and run deterministically, but no callback is produced by the submitted implementation.

problem_assessment.notes: The task is a fair cross-cutting transport/error-lifecycle change. The hidden multipart wrapper is somewhat stricter than the prompt about the helper's argument convention, but the decisive browser requirements follow from the prompt and visible shared Node/client architecture.

evidence: test_execution.log shows the verifier completed normally: baseline passed and the new run exited 5 after reporting 8 passes and 5 failures.

junit_new.xml attributes the three browser failures to test timeouts, while the Node size-limit and boundary tests pass; there is no bootstrap, import, dependency, or runtime crash in the browser cases.
The trajectory shows the agent inspected src/client.js and its XHR progress path, but only modified src/node/index.js and src/request-base.js; focused Node tests then passed.
environment_assessment.finding: No meaningful external blocker affected the verifier; the failure is explained by incomplete transport coverage in the implementation.
